paper.title: Hydrography of the Gulf of Mexico Using Autonomous Floats
paper.verification: Crossref metadata and abstract checked 2026-10-01; full text (publisher HTML) read 2026-10-01

period_match.paper_data: 706 casts to at least 1000 m (489 of them to 1500 m) from 14 autonomous profiling floats; CCAR and AVISO altimeter SSH
period_match.supplied_data: GLORYS12 reanalysis temperature, salinity and sea surface height, 0-2000 m

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: Subtropical Underwater, Antarctic Intermediate Water and North Atlantic Deep Water show east-west gradients consistent with sources in the Loop Current and the Yucatan Channel.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'Maps of characteristic water masses, including Subtropical Underwater, Antarctic Intermediate Water (AAIW), and North Atlantic Deep Water, showed gradients from east to west'. Full text, section 3 and Figs. 7-9: Subtropical Underwater is the salinity maximum between sigma-t 24.5 and 26.5, present where it exceeds 36.6; Antarctic Intermediate Water is the salinity minimum; North Atlantic Deep Water is mapped by the depth of the 27.715 sigma-theta surface and the temperature at 1283 m, from the casts that reach 1500 m.
criteria.how_to_test: Maps for July 2011-August 2015 of: the salinity maximum between sigma-t 24.5 and 26.5 (its depth and value, and the thickness of water with salinity of at least 36.6); the salinity minimum (depth and value); the depth of the 27.715 sigma-theta surface and the temperature near 1283 m. East-minus-west differences of each.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: signs exact; magnitudes +/-30%)

criteria.title: Finding 2
criteria.claim: The deep Gulf has a two-layer structure: isotherms are deeper in the Loop Current and its eddies and shallower in cyclones.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The two-layer nature of the deep Gulf shows isotherms being deeper in the warm anticyclonic LC and LC eddies and shallower in the cold cyclones.' Full text, section 2: altimeter SSH, with the basin-mean steric signal removed, is interpolated to each cast; above 17 cm marks the Loop Current and its eddies and below -10 cm marks cyclones. The 6 C isotherm divides the upper and lower layers.
criteria.how_to_test: Depth of the 6 C isotherm, and of other selected isotherms, composited by sea-surface-height class (above 17 cm; below -10 cm) after removing the basin-mean seasonal signal from sea surface height.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: signs exact)

criteria.title: Finding 3
criteria.claim: The mean seasonal mixed-layer depth has a maximum of about 60 m in January and a minimum of about 20 m in June-July.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'Mixed layer depths have an average seasonal signal that shows maximum depths (~60 m) in January and a minimum in June-July (~20 m).' Full text, sections 3 and 5: the mixed-layer depth follows de Boyer Montegut et al. (2004), searching down from the 10 m value to a temperature difference of 0.2 C or a density difference of 0.03 kg m-3. The temperature criterion gives slightly deeper values; both have maxima in December-January and minima in June-July.
criteria.how_to_test: Deep-basin mixed-layer depth climatology for July 2011-August 2015 with both criteria from a 10 m reference (0.2 C; 0.03 kg m-3), or a stated alternative.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: months +/-1; depths +/-15 m)

criteria.title: Finding 4
criteria.claim: Basin-mean steric height from 0-50 m dynamic height and sea surface height have a seasonal range of about 12 cm, with significant interannual variability.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'Basin-mean steric heights from 0-50-m dynamic heights and altimeter SSH show a seasonal range of ~12 cm, with significant interannual variability.' Full text, section 5 and Fig. 13: the steric signal of sea surface height is its daily deep-water average; it is compared with the monthly 0-50 m height equivalent (dynamic height divided by gravity) averaged over the float locations.
criteria.how_to_test: Seasonal range of the deep-water mean sea surface height and of the basin-mean 0-50 m height equivalent (dynamic height divided by gravity); year-to-year differences in the summer maxima and winter minima.

criteria.title: Finding 5
criteria.claim: The translation of Loop Current eddies across the western basin produces a region of low, homogeneous potential vorticity over its deepest part.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The translation of LC eddies across the western basin produces a region of low homogeneous potential vorticity centered over the deepest part of the western basin.' Full text, section 6 and Fig. 16: lower-layer potential vorticity is f/h6, where h6 is the water depth minus the depth of the 6 C isotherm. The lowest values are nearly uniform and coincide with the deep cyclonic gyre; they result from the bowl-shaped bathymetry and the deepening of the mean deep isotherms along the eddy paths.
criteria.how_to_test: Testable: the mean depth of the 6 C isotherm and whether it deepens over the western basin along the paths of Loop Current eddies. Not testable directly: f/h6 itself needs the water depth, and the supplied fields stop at 2000 m with no bathymetry.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: location of the deepest mean 6 C isotherm within 1.5 degrees; sign exact)

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: Water-mass definitions (the salinity maximum between sigma-t 24.5 and 26.5 above 36.6; the salinity minimum; the 27.715 sigma-theta surface); the mixed-layer criteria (0.2 C and 0.03 kg m-3 from the 10 m value); the 0-50 m height equivalent and the deep-water mean sea surface height; lower-layer potential vorticity f/h6 below the 6 C isotherm; sea-surface-height classes (above 17 cm, below -10 cm, steric signal removed); the deep-basin mask.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: A gridded reanalysis versus 706 float casts (different sampling in space and time); the reanalysis assimilates such profiles, so agreement is not independent; reanalysis sea surface height versus altimetry; the casts reach 1000 m (489 of them 1500 m) while the supplied fields reach 2000 m; no bathymetry is supplied.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
